L2_asset_class_replay_vs_episode_actual_.question: How does L2 asset-class replay differ from evidence tied to the episode's actual asset?
L2_asset_class_replay_vs_episode_actual_.finding: world.py's comment at _asset_type_from_id (line ~108) explicitly warns: "'metro_pump_1' and 'hydraulic_pump_1' are both pumps, but that must come from the registry's own asset_type/equipment_type field, not a naive substring match." This documents intent to distinguish an asset's TYPE (e.g. 'pump') from its INSTANCE (e.g. 'metro_pump_1' vs 'hydraulic_pump_1'), consistent with L2 being asset-class-level replay evidence (e.g. a real recording from A pump, not necessarily THIS pump instance) versus an episode's actual/L1 instance-specific evidence. The registry file itself (robot_assets_registry.json, referenced by world.py's docstring) was NOT FOUND in this repository (searched with find -iname across the whole tree, 0 results) -- it likely lives in one of the sibling working directories (AssetOpsBenchScenarioGeneration, inspection-world) not audited this pass. Cannot confirm the exact asset_type values it resolves to, or whether they total 6.
L2_asset_class_replay_vs_episode_actual_.status: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED -- the conceptual distinction is documented in code comments, but the registry data needed to fully resolve it (and to check the '6 asset types' claim against it) was NOT FOUND in this repository.

does_benchmark_support_explicit_provenan: PARTIALLY. A provenance mechanism exists in two forms: (1) a runtime L1/L2/L3/NOT_APPLICABLE_DIGITAL_ENTERPRISE/SIMULATED_UNCLASSIFIED evidence-source tier defined in World (world.py) but not found persisted in the current V3 canonical manifests; (2) a generation-time lineage provenance (world_id, matched_group_id, generator_version, schema_version, fingerprint -- for A/E/C/D) and an explicit source_provenance block (for 50/66 B-Acquisition episodes: source_id, source_dataset, modality, asset, scenario_family, benchmark_family, world_id, episode_id, provenance_class). Both exist and are real, but they are NOT the same mechanism, and neither one alone spans the full 4,075-episode benchmark with a uniform schema. An abstract claim of 'evidence with explicit provenance' is defensible only if scoped to describe form (2) (lineage/generation-time provenance, present on effectively all canonical episodes) or explicitly caveated for form (1) (evidence-source tiering, confirmed present in code but not confirmed populated across the persisted V3 manifest).
